parsed.notes: Lens B only; no support or quote-fidelity findings were made.

reasons: Lake identity is verified for Hampton v. United States, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1976-04-27.
Lake citations include 425 U.S. 484, 96 S. Ct. 1646, 48 L. Ed. 2d 113, and 1976 U.S. LEXIS 49.
Lake treatment field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30, so the disclosed record does not show the authority is dead law.
residual_risks: Treatment derivation contains proposed negative/audit candidates, but no final lake judgment invalidates the authority.

defect.evidence_quote: Plurality opinion (Rehnquist, J.); Powell & Blackmun concurred in the judgment on narrower grounds.
defect.problem: The holding label should not state the due-process no-bar rationale as an unqualified binding holding; disclosed treatment says the opinion was a plurality and Powell/Blackmun concurred only on narrower grounds.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise the holding to separate the binding entrapment/predisposition judgment from the plurality due-process rationale, e.g. 'Entrapment is unavailable to a predisposed defendant; in the plurality's view, due process also did not bar conviction where the government supplied contraband.'

reasons: Lens B does not challenge factual support or quote fidelity.
The disclosed treatment scope note limits the precedential force of the due-process portion.
residual_risks: Lens A should separately verify the holding text and any omitted ending after the ellipsis.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the plurality/narrow-concurrence caveat directly in the holding field.

reasons: For currency/treatment, the lake record keeps Hampton as good_law as of 2026-06-30.
The lake progeny fields show 628 indexed citing opinions and citation_count 911, supporting current significance for an entrapment/progeny role.
Nothing in the disclosed final treatment fields overrules, abrogates, or supersedes Hampton.
residual_risks: The editorial label 'Key' is partly judgmental; Lens B only confirms the case is not stale or invalidated.

reasons: Lake identity lists court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus.
A SCOTUS authority supports the case-level weight label Binding — SCOTUS.
The plurality caveat affects point-level precedential force, not the case-level court weight label.
residual_risks: Individual propositions still need the plurality/narrow-concurrence caveat.

reasons: The content treatment fields match the lake treatment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 1976-04-27, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, composite_basis migration-seed, varies_by_point false, and the same scope_note.

Lake point_overrides is empty and all listed treatment edges are marked proposed with field_iii mentioned, so the disclosed final judgment does not show Hampton has been overruled, abrogated, superseded, or limited as a validity matter.
The scope_note adequately discloses the plurality/narrow-concurrence limitation.
residual_risks: Lake derivation reports audit_needed and proposed negative events in lane1/lane2; these are residual audit risks, not final negative treatment in the disclosed record.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If the rendered page says 'No negative treatment,' tighten to 'No final negative treatment recorded in the lake; proposed audit candidates remain.'
